newsitem.title: USA: Prince George's Cty to spur economic development.
newsitem.headline: Prince George's Cty to spur economic development.

text.p: Prince George's County, Md., officials are looking to pump up the local economy and are looking to business leaders to do the bulk of the heavy lifting, the Washington Post reported Thursday.

The county's publicly funded Economic Development Corp. on Thursday is expected to announce a campaign to raise $1.5 million over the next five years from local businesses to lure companies to the area and assist existing firms in expanding their operations, the Post reported.
The county is seeking money from businesses because it has been unable to raise spending for economic development over the past four years, the Post reported.
The campaign already has netted pledges of $775,000 from executives at companies including Washington Gas and Light Co. and Winchester Homes.

A tight budget is forcing the county to seek the help of corporations. The proposed $300,000 annually would allow the county to heighten its public relations campaign about the benefits of doing business in Prince George's County.

The goal for 1997 is to generate private investment of $161 million through businesses expanding and coming to Prince George's -- which is expected to lead to 2,000 new jobs and retention of 2,000 jobs.
